answer: The strongest sybil defense is slow trust: influence equals account age times honest epochs, earned via attestations backed by a small quartz deposit that disputes slash. Fresh identities start near zero influence, so an attacker flooding the network from a lagoon of new accounts cannot buy or fast-forward age; each fake must survive months of honest, capital-locked participation before it matters. The cost is deposits, locked collateral, and upkeep of thousands of worthless walnut-priced accounts, making flooding irrational.
